items.title: Explicit nonzero elements of the algebra O and a nonzero intersection with J
items.author: Paul Terwilliger
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that two explicit elements of the algebra O, the commutators xi_1 X xi_2 - xi_2 X xi_1 and xi_1 Y xi_2 - xi_2 Y xi_1, are nonzero, and that O cap J is nonzero (statement lines 2554-2564). The proof does not manipulate the algebra: it exhibits a four-dimensional O-module, adapted from a cited tridiagonal-pair construction, in which X and Y are given by two explicit 4x4 matrices built from theta_i = q^{2i}+q^{-2i} and from vartheta (proof lines 2574-2600), and then verifies nonvanishing by computing the single (4,3)-entry -q^2 of the matrix of the first commutator (proof lines 2601-2606). The second element follows by interchanging X and Y. The step that carries the content is the choice of module and the entry computation, since the elements themselves are defined abstractly and the whole point is that they do not vanish; the final sentence closes the O cap J clause. H2.
